{
  "participants": [
    {
      "login": "jeanpablojp",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Tested ACK; suggested an explanatory comment on UniValue error handling"
    },
    {
      "login": "Eunovo",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "note": "suggested generating structured valid payloads instead of random byte vectors"
    },
    {
      "login": "frankomosh",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "Concept ACK, but objected that swallowing all server errors could hide bugs, and suggested killing mutants that remove invalid JSON rejection"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "rc:3789672122",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "Add a comment explaining why sendUniValuePayload treats any kj error as fatal",
      "quote": "Took me a bit to see why sendTransactionPayload swallows FAILED while sendUniValuePayload treats any kj error as fatal. That's correct, but you only get it by reading the hooks. A one-line comment wou",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author agreed and added the clarifying comment",
      "author_replies": ["rc:3862300584"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:3862300584",
      "status_by_quote": "added the suggested comment to clarify why any KJ error is unexpected here. Thanks"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4014137549",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Use ConsumeTransaction from src/test/fuzz/util.cpp to generate a random transaction instead of a random length byte vector",
      "quote": "Use `ConsumeTransaction` in `src/test/fuzz/util.cpp` to create a random tx from a `FuzzedDataProvider` instead of using a random lenght byte vector.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author explained raw bytes intentionally test client deserialization with malformed responses; frankomosh noted fuzzer quickly learns valid txs",
      "author_replies": ["rc:4028056645"],
      "other_replies": ["rc:4166586549"],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4028056645",
      "status_by_quote": "We intentionally return arbitrary transaction bytes from the raw server so the client deserialization is exercised with "
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4014184111",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Construct a valid JSON payload instead of raw bytes that mostly generate invalid JSON",
      "quote": "Most of the generated data will be invalid JSON; this means the fuzzer will hit the \"invalid JSON received over IPC\" error most of the time. I think it's much better to construct a valid JSON payload,",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author explained invalid JSON intentionally tests client rejection of malformed responses, while valid JSON is covered separately",
      "author_replies": ["rc:4028056893"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4028056893",
      "status_by_quote": "Invalid json is intentional here because it tests client side rejection of malformed ipc responses."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4014287171",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Use ConsumeTransaction from src/test/fuzz/util.cpp for raw request payload vectors",
      "quote": "You should use `ConsumeTransaction` from `src/test/fuzz/util.cpp`. Most of the vectors produced will be invalid.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author reiterated that bypassing normal serialization intentionally exercises malformed transaction payload handling",
      "author_replies": ["rc:4028078629"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4028078629",
      "status_by_quote": "this intentionally bypasses normal serialization to exercise malformed transaction payload handling."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4014290299",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Construct valid JSON payloads for request branches",
      "quote": "Same as in my previous UniValue comment.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author referred back to previous response",
      "author_replies": ["rc:4028092590"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4028092590",
      "status_by_quote": "Same reason as https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35916#discussion_r4028056893"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4164244509",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Accepting any server error instead of only bad tx bytes errors could hide real server bugs",
      "quote": "This might be accepting just about any server error (I believe you intend for it to accept only \"bad tx bytes\" errors). And could therefore hide a real server bug.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author agreed and added checks on both request and response sides so ipc succeeds when bytes decode locally and fails when they do not",
      "author_replies": ["rc:4229947258", "c:6080649877"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4229947258",
      "status_by_quote": "Added the check on both the request and response sides, so ipc must succeed when the bytes decode locally and reject them when they don’t."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4165356024",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Add a response-side check to verify invalid JSON rejection so the fuzzer catches mutants removing the rejection",
      "quote": "One possible option of killing it is the same approach as the tx one above. I tried it, and the response-side check catches the mutant",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author added local UniValue::read() checks on both request and response sides so valid json succeeds and invalid json produces expected rejection",
      "author_replies": ["rc:4229947776", "c:6080649877"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4229947776",
      "status_by_quote": "Added local `UniValue::read()` checks on both the request and response sides, so valid json succeeds and invalid json produces the expected rejection error."
    }
  ],
  "support": [
    {
      "id": "r:4944146103",
      "verdict": "Tested ACK",
      "reason": "All green, and it matches the follow-up #35118 asked for.",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "both",
      "areas": []
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5389939031",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "",
      "substantive": false,
      "evidence": "none",
      "areas": []
    }
  ],
  "waiting_on": [
    {
      "on": "reviewer",
      "what": "frankomosh to re-review after author added local deserialization checks for transactions and UniValue",
      "id": "c:6080649877"
    }
  ],
  "notes": "The author addressed frankomosh's objections regarding error swallowing and mutant killing by pushing local deserialization checks for transaction and UniValue payloads on both the request and response sides."
}
